chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: Recording pay and who handled the business
summary: Record pay came months later via the leader with no bonus; Russell handled the business and musicians simply received what they were promised.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: How much did you get paid for recording, and...?
Well, we won't go into the pay now. No-no-no, don't go into that. I can't have my feelings hurt again.
And from whom did you get paid? Usually from the bandleader?
Well, the money I think was paid by the studio, the company you worked for.
But you didn't collect then and there?

It would be from three to six months gettin' paid. Three to six months later. No, you didn't get it then and there. But I think we did get paid for "Can't Give You Anything But Love." We got paid right away for that. I think so, yeah. But the rest of the numbers, we had to wait until they did the rest of the recording. You had to wait in them days for your money.
And Russell handled all the business, right?
He taken care of the business, yeah.
So as long as you were in his band, you got then a bonus for the recordings later? Or how did you know what was for the recordings and what was your salary?

You got paid whatever you were promised. Sometimes you got it, sometimes you didn't. But what you got, that was for your record. And that was the end of your record, as far as you were concerned. You got paid for making a record and that was it. No bonus, no nothin', no... Now, the rest of it, that's between the leader, the leader of the band or the star or the big-shots, between them... It had nothing to do with the musicians. The musicians just made the date, and got their little salary, whatever they was promised to get, and that was the end of it.
